summary: tavern-ai-sdk ships hidden obfuscated loader and sandbox-detection native addon on import
details: Package is advertised as a persona-JSON loader exposing getPersona/listPersonas/personaIds over 8 persona cards, but the published tarball additionally ships four large single-line hex-identifier obfuscated JS bundles (cache-warm.mjs ~296KB, build-cache.mjs ~203KB, cache-sweep.mjs ~300KB, workspaces.js ~288KB) and multi-platform native N-API binaries at native/{linux,darwin,win32}/{arm64,x64}/cache-probe.node. The main entry personas.mjs statically imports cache-warm.mjs, so the obfuscated code runs on require('tavern-ai-sdk'). The bundles reference createRequire, child_process, spawn, exec, and aws-prefixed strings — a code-execution and cloud-credential surface wholly unrelated to loading persona JSON. The cache-probe.node binaries are built from the open-source VMAware library (symbol../VMAware/src/vmaware.hpp, VMDetect::GetCallback) and probe for QEMU, VirtualBox, VMware, Hyper-V, KVM, Docker, WSL, Azure, GCE, AWS Nitro, Qihoo360 sandbox, ThreatExpert, Hybrid Analysis, BlueStacks and similar via SMBIOS/CPUID/dmidecode/ioreg/sysctl. The bundle headers self-label as "build cache manifest. Restore from package-lock if corrupted," and the file names (cache-warm, cache-sweep, build-cache, workspaces, cache-probe) are chosen to look like routine build infrastructure, but none of these artifacts implement or are needed by the advertised persona-loader API. The combination — obfuscated import-time-reachable code with child_process/exec and cloud-SDK fingerprints, gated behind native anti-analysis VM/sandbox detection, under a cover-story name — is the canonical shape of a staged credential-stealer that withholds its payload inside analysis environments.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
